messages:
Sam: Stormport sent an RFI addendum. They want a single-page capability matrix + explicit burst billing, regional peering notes, and a short POC acceptance checklist. They want the packet by Wed COB.
Priya: Copy. Legal wants precise language on HSM compatibility: we must state "compatible with FIPS-validated HSMs" not that we are FIPS-certified. Also require SOC2 cert and a statement on key rotation (default 90 days).
Leo: Perf numbers proposal (conservative): Hosted: 45 QPS sustained @512 tokens (p95 ~230ms); Dedicated (4xA100 equiv): 320 QPS sustained, handle 8-10x short bursts with autoscale and graceful shed; Private: provide ranges and note depends on customer infra.
Harper: For regional peering/residency they asked for EU/US/APAC latencies and routing guarantees. We can list per-region sustained QPS and that hosted routing honors data residency flags; Private can be deployed inside customer VPC.
Sam: Billing formula draft: burst_fee = base_rate * excess_multiplier * minutes_billed * burst_multiplier. Define excess_multiplier = (burst_QPS/commit_QPS - 1), burst_multiplier = 2.5. Add one-line numeric example.
Leo: Example to paste: commit=300 QPS, burst=1200 QPS for 6 minutes -> excess_multiplier=3 -> minutes_billed=6 -> burst_fee = base_rate * 3 * 6 * 2.5.
Priya: Also include POC acceptance criteria: 1) sustained throughput test (two runs) within 10% of committed QPS; 2) p95 latency under target for both runs; 3) failover test: regional fallback completes within SLO. Keep it short and measurable.
BenchBot: bench-job stormport-5067778888 started on ephemeral infra; ETA 50m for p50/p95/p99 and batch assumptions.
Harper: Action items: Leo update one-pager matrix with regional columns and quantization row (8-bit supported, 4-bit experimental); Priya attach SOC2 excerpt and BYOK wording; Sam assemble the packet and upload to the Stormport folder. Drop assets by 16:00 PT Tue.
Sam: Sounds good 97 I'll assemble and include a short note on autoscale smoothing window (30s) and graceful throttle policy. Ping here for blockers. :thumbsup:
